title: A nonempty scheme is connected iff its global sections have only the idempotents 0 and 1
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Then $X$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] if and only if the only idempotent elements $e=e^2$ of the ring $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ of global sections of its structure sheaf are $e=0$ and $e=1$.

source.place: Lemma 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections), proof of part (2): 'If $X=Y\amalg Z$ with $Y$ and $Z$ open in $X$, then we obtain an idempotent $e\in A$ by taking the section of $\mathcal O_X$ which is $1$ on $Y$ and $0$ on $Z$.
